transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood Eng), Emma (Lakeview), Rafael (Lakeview CTO), Sophie (Lakeview)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics — streaming, param tuning (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), and retries/robustness. Customer is evaluating hosted first to move quickly, likely pilot then Dedicated or Private depending on compliance.

[00:00] Jared: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jared from Redwood Inference, i'll kick off then pass to priya for an end-to-end demo. can folks introduce?
[00:07] Emma: hi all, emma here, head of ml at lakeview, we own model infra selection for analytics features.
[00:11] Rafael: rafael, cto, i'll be involved for infra/security questions.
[00:15] Sophie: sophie, handles platform and networking.
[00:19] Priya: great thanks, quick agenda: 1) Hosted API basics, 2) live demo of chat/text generation and streaming, 3) param tuning and cost/latency tradeoffs, 4) retries and error handling patterns, 5) q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Emma: yes sounds good.

[02:05] Priya: okay starting on the hosted api — simple REST + SDK (python/js) for chat, text, embeddings. here is example python snippet:
    # pseudocode shown verbally
    resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-1-chat", messages=msgs, temperature=0.2, max_tokens=512, stream=True)
    for chunk in resp: handle_chunk(chunk)
  (note: snippets in recorder may be rough)

[04:10] Marcus: two points to call out: streaming reduces tail latency for user-facing chat, and we support token-level events so you can render partial responses as they arrive.

[06:00] Rafael: can you talk about default retries and idempotency? our infra needs deterministic behaviors for retries so we don't double-bill or duplicate actions.
[06:12] Priya: yeah good question. hosted api supports request_id and idempotency keys. our SDK will do safe retries for 5xx with exponential backoff; we recommend client-side dedupe for multi-step operations. also we surfaced retry budgets on the console.

[08:30] Emma: what's typical latency for streaming? and how does batching affect cost?
[08:40] Priya: for short convs (<200 tokens) p95 is around 200-400ms for token start, then streaming tokens follow at model throughput. batching helps throughput/cost for high qps but adds a small extra latency window — we can tune batching windows. (note: numbers are approximate, final perf depends on model & input).

[10:55] Priya: demo time — i've got the console open (redwood console). starting a live chat call via the hosted playground, you can see streaming chunks arrive in the UI. i'll also run the python sdk snippet in a small demo app.
[12:15] (audio: typing, brief pause)
[12:22] Priya: okay sending prompt: "Summarize Q3 revenue trends and highlight anomalies for a finance dashboard." watch the UI stream the response, chunk by chunk.
[13:00] (streaming text appears)
[13:10] Priya: you'll see partial segments, then finalization with finish_reason. console also shows latency per token and token counts for cost insight.

[15:05] Marcus: on params: temperature controls randomness (0.0 = deterministic, 1.0 = more creative). top_p is nucleus sampling — we use either, not both typically. max_tokens limits output; stop sequences for structured outputs. we also expose penalty params (presence/ frequency) for repetition control.

[18:00] Sophie: how do you recommend setting these for our use-case? we generate executive summaries and follow-up bullet points — need concise accurate output.
[18:10] Priya: for concise summaries we'd start with temperature 0.0-0.2, max_tokens 150-300, and maybe presence_penalty 0.0 freq_penalty 0.2. also use system prompts to anchor tone and format. we can share a prompt cookbook.

[20:40] Emma: billing curiosity — how does token billing work with streaming? are partial tokens billed?
[20:50] Jared: billing is per input + output tokens; streaming is just transport, billing happens on the final consumed tokens. if you stop early, you only pay for tokens generated up to that point. console shows token-level breakdown.

[22:30] Rafael: security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS for keys, and data residency for EU customers. what's available on hosted?
[22:45] Priya: hosted supports SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and integration with customer KMS for dedicated/private. for hosted we have strong controls and SOC2 compliance — i'll attach our SOC2 report and a security checklist. for data residency we have regional endpoints and can restrict routing; for strict residency or on-prem you can use Private.

[25:00] Sophie: networking — can hosted connect to our VPC or do we need Private for VPC peering?
[25:10] Priya: hosted is public API; for VPC peering and private connectivity we recommend Redwood Private or dedicated-hosting with VPC options — for pilots many customers start hosted then move to dedicated/private when they require peering.

[27:30] Marcus: on reliability: we have multi-variant fallbacks — you can configure routing policies (latency-first, cost-first) and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constrained. this helps maintain availability during spikes.

[29:00] Emma: curious about model versions and rollouts — can we pin a model for a route and do canary?
[29:10] Priya: yes, route-level model pinning and canary rollouts are supported in the console. you can set weights, monitor latency & quality, and rollback automatically.

[31:40] Rafael: what's typical throughput for dedicated offering? we have peak batch jobs at 300 concurrent streams during reporting windows.
[31:50] Marcus: dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies; we can size based on tokens/sec and concurrency. we'll need to run a benchmark with your sample prompts to give a precise sizing.

[33:20] Emma: about retries — can you show a failure pattern and how app should handle it?
[33:30] Priya: sure, i'll simulate a transient 503. recommended pattern: exponential backoff with jitter, limit retries to 3-4, idempotency keys for non-idempotent ops, and fallback to a smaller model or cached response if latency SLO is at risk. console includes retry metrics and you can set alerting on retry rates.

[35:05] Sophie: any client-side utilities for batching or KV cache? we have a lot of repeated prefixes across chat sessions.
[35:15] Marcus: we expose kv-cache hooks for session caching in private runtimes; hosted offers prefix caching heuristics and we also have suggestions from Redwood Optimize for batching windows and caching config. Optimize will recommend quantization/model variants too.

[37:40] Priya: demo wrap-up — quick run through of error logs in the console (showing stack traces/ request ids) and where to find docs. we also linked a sample benchmark spreadsheet that shows tokens/sec, cost estimates under different batch sizes.

[39:00] Emma: this was helpful. next steps?
[39:05] Jared: action items — i'll send pricing + pilot agreement, priya will share SOC2 and network diagram. we'll run a benchmark: customer to provide sample prompts and a small anonymized dataset. propose pilot start week of 2026-12-08?
[39:30] Rafael: that timeline works tentatively. we'll confirm internal approvals.

[40:00] Priya: ok i'll follow up with links to quickstart repo, python/js sdk examples, and a prompt cookbook.
[40:10] Jared: thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email.
[41:45] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash), some names may be mis-typed, system-level numbers are approximate.
